notes: Canonical claim dispositions. Assessment and confidence are separate; deprecated historical material remains visible only behind the generated provenance boundary.

claims.statement: Google publicly frames local results using relevance, distance, and prominence/popularity; these are not an exhaustive public formula.
claims.scope: Google local results; feature and locale availability vary

claims.statement: Google does not publish universal weights, thresholds, or guaranteed lifts for local ranking factors.
claims.scope: Google local results

claims.statement: A service-area business that does not serve customers at its address should remove or hide that address; storefront eligibility requires a real customer-facing location.
claims.scope: Google Business Profile; region-specific options may vary

claims.statement: A rented mailing or virtual-office address where the business does not operate is ineligible; a coworking storefront requires permanent signage, customer reception, and the business's own staff during stated hours.
claims.scope: Google Business Profile eligibility

claims.statement: A Business Profile should use the real-world name and the fewest accurate categories needed to describe its core business; fixed category quotas are not official doctrine.
claims.scope: Google Business Profile

claims.statement: Verification evidence must truthfully demonstrate business location, existence, and management. Video verification must be captured live, unique and unedited, and exclude sensitive information and other people’s faces.
claims.scope: Google Business Profile verification

claims.statement: Google Maps and Business Profile reviews prohibit incentives for posting, revising, or removing reviews, even when disclosed. Fake, gated, quota-driven, conflict-of-interest, selectively positive, or wording-manipulated reviews are prohibited.
claims.scope: Google Maps and Business Profile contributions

claims.statement: Prompts and workflows must not fabricate firsthand experiences, identities, costs, awards, guarantees, reviews, or community posts.
claims.scope: Local SEO Brain outputs and Google user-contributed content

claims.statement: No reviewed official source establishes a universal twice-weekly GBP post requirement, 30-day ranking decay cliff, or mandatory photo cadence.
claims.scope: Google Business Profile posts; category and region vary

claims.statement: No reviewed official source establishes a universal 24-hour review-reply deadline or a direct local-ranking lift from reply speed.
claims.scope: Google Business Profile reviews

claims.statement: The My Business Q&A API was discontinued on 2025-11-03, but that does not establish a universal sunset of consumer place Q&A or prove Ask Maps replaced it everywhere.
claims.scope: API versus consumer UI; locale, device, account, and category vary

claims.statement: Ask Maps launched as a conversational place-discovery experience with an initial U.S. and India mobile rollout; Google did not document it as a universal replacement for Business Profile Q&A.
claims.scope: Launch scope as of 2026-03-12

claims.statement: Google documents no additional technical requirements, mandatory special schema, or AI text file for eligibility in AI Overviews or AI Mode beyond ordinary Search requirements and policies.
claims.scope: Google Search AI features

claims.statement: Two independent observational datasets associate AI-summary result pages with fewer clicks to external/traditional results; no single percentage should be generalized across query sets.
claims.scope: Pew U.S. panel and Ahrefs informational-query dataset; not universal

claims.statement: Fixed AI citation counts, Reddit citation-share percentages, and guaranteed local AIO tactics are unsupported across platforms, query classes, locales, and dates.
claims.scope: AI search platforms and local query classes

claims.statement: Google documents worldwide availability of Search Console Generative AI performance reporting as of 2026-08-31. It exposes impressions for AI Overviews and AI Mode by page, country, date, and device; dedicated AI-feature click or query reporting is not established by the reviewed documentation.
claims.scope: Worldwide documented availability from 2026-08-31; AI Overviews and AI Mode impression dimensions; feature data limitations

claims.statement: Google Search supports JSON-LD, Microdata, and RDFa for structured data; JSON-LD is recommended for maintainability but is not the only supported format.
claims.scope: Google Search structured data

claims.statement: Valid structured data creates feature eligibility and can help understanding, but Google does not guarantee rich-result appearance or document a direct organic-rank or AI-citation lift.
claims.scope: Google Search

claims.statement: Schema.org defines vocabulary and its validator checks vocabulary/syntax; Google documentation and the Rich Results Test govern Google feature eligibility.
claims.scope: Schema.org vocabulary versus Google Search features

claims.statement: Self-serving reviews on an entity's own LocalBusiness or Organization pages are ineligible for Google star review features; ratings must not be aggregated from other sites.
claims.scope: Google review rich results

claims.statement: FAQ rich results stopped appearing in Google Search as of 2026-05-07; FAQ markup must not be sold as a current ordinary rich-result or AI-growth tactic.
claims.scope: Google Search rich results

claims.statement: Google documents evolved PageRank and link-analysis systems as only part of its ranking systems; fixed authority-point arithmetic and placement weights are unsupported.
claims.scope: Google organic Search ranking

claims.statement: Google documents no preferred universal word count, keyword density, publication cadence, or fixed page-count framework; content should be people-first and useful for its purpose.
claims.scope: Google organic Search

claims.statement: Google documents no magical ideal internal or external link count; links should be useful, contextual, crawlable, and appropriately qualified.
claims.scope: Google organic Search

claims.statement: PBNs, paid ranking links without qualification, optimized forum/comment links, and link networks created primarily to manipulate ranking violate Google's spam policies.
claims.scope: Google Web Search

claims.statement: Hidden text used to manipulate ranking, doorway pages, and scaled low-value location/content pages violate Google's spam policies.
claims.scope: Google Web Search

claims.statement: User-facing accordions and tabs are not automatically hidden-content abuse when they serve ordinary design and user-experience purposes.
claims.scope: Google Web Search

claims.statement: EXIF can represent image metadata, including GPS data, but no reviewed source establishes that GPS geotagging causes Google local or organic ranking gains.
claims.scope: Google Search and Business Profile images

claims.statement: Core Web Vitals are used within page-experience systems, but passing them does not guarantee ranking and relevance can outweigh page experience.
claims.scope: Google organic Search

claims.statement: Aggregated interaction data has been described in primary trial evidence, but this does not validate GA bounce-rate formulas, dwell-time thresholds, CTR manipulation, or local-ranking guarantees.
claims.scope: Google Search interaction systems; no site-level formula

claims.statement: Generative-engine optimization experiments show bounded, domain- and platform-dependent effects; citation breadth and answer influence are distinct, so universal GEO recipes are not established.
claims.scope: Benchmarks and evolving AI platforms

claims.statement: A causal Yelp study found a 5–9% revenue effect from a one-star increase for independent restaurants in its historical Washington State sample; it does not establish Google ranking effects or universal industry outcomes.
claims.scope: Yelp independent restaurants; historical Washington State sample

claims.statement: Places content is subject to attribution, storage, caching, and license restrictions; competitor discovery does not authorize a permanent raw Places-content vault.
claims.scope: Google Maps Platform Places content

claims.statement: Local SEO Brain is advisory: any account control or third-party mutation requires explicit owner approval, scoped execution, and a rollback path.
claims.scope: Local SEO Brain product behavior

claims.statement: Local SEO Brain ingests authorized exports and drafts evidence-linked recommendations; it does not mutate Google or third-party accounts.
claims.scope: Local SEO Brain v0.3.0

claims.statement: When source data is absent, synthesis must report Draft or no-data status and must not fabricate a grade, score, metric, causal explanation, or completed action.
claims.scope: Local SEO Brain synthesis

claims.statement: Derived review notes omit review-author identity; authorized raw exports remain immutable and access-controlled rather than being copied into public deliverables.
claims.scope: Local SEO Brain review ingestion

claims.statement: A pinned as-of date and canonical overlay/ledger inputs deterministically regenerate reviewed note metadata and evidence callouts without editing the historical raw seed.
claims.scope: Local SEO Brain build pipeline

claims.statement: Original licensed seed bytes remain immutable provenance in .raw. Working notes are rewritten current guidance; historical prescriptions must not be treated as current evidence.
claims.scope: All generated seed chapters and prompt notes
claims.notes: This disposition preserves licensed history while preventing it from being treated as current doctrine.

claims.statement: Google permits generative AI as a content-production aid. Generating many pages without user value may violate scaled-content-abuse policy; content and metadata should be manually checked for accuracy and trustworthiness, with creation context when useful to readers.
claims.scope: global; content production and Search policy

claims.statement: From 2026-08-30, site-reputation-policy manual-action effects differ by searcher location. Outside the EEA the affected portion can be directly impacted; inside the EEA that manual-action impact does not apply, though the portion may be separated and ranked independently.
claims.scope: EEA versus non-EEA searcher location; enforcement, not permission to create spam

claims.statement: Google aggregator and supplier units support EEA local-business queries. Aggregators require approved vertical-search-service status and data integration. Suppliers are direct providers serving EEA users and appear only alongside an aggregator unit.
claims.scope: EEA; named Search units, not universal Map Pack eligibility

claims.statement: For Google Search review-snippet eligibility, fake or undisclosed incentivized reviews are prohibited; a provided benefit must be clearly and prominently disclosed. This does not relax Maps incentive prohibitions or guarantee rich results.
claims.scope: Google Search review markup versus Maps review policy

claims.statement: From 2026-07-24, My Business API v4.9 documents reviewReplyUrl retrieval through reviews get, list, and batchGetReviews.
claims.scope: API field documentation only; no Local SEO Brain live integration

claims.statement: From 2026-10-09, My Business API v4.9 documents GLUTEN_FREE and DAIRY_FREE DietaryRestriction values for food-menu items through getFoodMenus and updateFoodMenus.
claims.scope: API enum and method documentation only; no live account integration

claims.statement: The Search Status Dashboard records August and September 2026 spam updates in addition to earlier named events. Rollout dates alone do not establish why an individual site moved.
claims.scope: named historical events through review date; no causal diagnosis

claims.statement: The operator workflow is to inventory authorized evidence, separate observed facts from hypotheses, draft a scoped finding with sources and missing inputs, and obtain owner approval and a rollback plan for any proposed external change.
claims.scope: Local SEO Brain operator procedure; practitioner recommendation

claims.statement: Google describes E-E-A-T as a quality-assessment concept, not a specific ranking factor. Accurate authorship, sourcing, and demonstrated experience can help readers assess trust.
claims.scope: Google Search people-first quality guidance; no score or ranking formula

claims.statement: Google recommends clear, concise, accurate, page-specific titles and short, unique meta descriptions. Search snippets can use page content rather than the supplied description.
claims.scope: Google Search title links and snippets; no display or click guarantee

claims.statement: Business Profile information should accurately represent real operations. Descriptions, service offerings, and normal or special hours need owner-confirmed facts.
claims.scope: Business Profile representation; proposed field edits require owner approval
